sentences.zh: 薛淵

translations.literal: Xue Yuan
translations.idiomatic: Xue Yuan

sentences.zh: 薛淵，河東汾陰人也。

translations.literal: Xue Yuan was a native of Fenyin in Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Yuan was a man of Fenyin in Hedong.

sentences.zh: 宋徐州刺史安都從子。

translations.literal: He was a nephew of An Du, Song's inspector of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was nephew to An Du, inspector of Xuzhou under the Song.

sentences.zh: 本名道淵，避太祖偏諱改。

translations.literal: His original name was Dao Yuan; to avoid the Founder's partial taboo he changed it.
translations.idiomatic: His birth name was Dao Yuan; he changed it to avoid the Founder's taboo on the character yuan.

sentences.zh: 安都以彭城降虜，親族皆入北。

translations.literal: When An Du surrendered Pengcheng to the northerners, his kin all went north.
translations.idiomatic: When An Du gave up Pengcheng to the northern enemy, the whole clan went north.

sentences.zh: 太祖鎮淮陰，淵遁來南，委身自結。

translations.literal: While the Founder held Huaiyin, Yuan fled south and pledged himself in close bond.
translations.idiomatic: While the Founder was posted at Huaiyin, Yuan stole south and threw himself on the Founder's favor.

sentences.zh: 果幹有氣力。

translations.literal: He was resolute and capable, full of physical strength.
translations.idiomatic: He was bold and able, with great bodily strength.

sentences.zh: 太祖使領部曲，備衞帳內，從征伐。

translations.literal: The Founder had him lead his own followers, guard the inner camp, and take part in campaigns.
translations.idiomatic: The Founder set him at the head of his household troops, guarding the inner quarters, and sent him on campaign after campaign.

sentences.zh: 元徽末，以勳官至輔國將軍，右軍將軍，驍騎將軍、軍主，封竟陵侯。

translations.literal: Late in the Yuanhui era, by merit he rose to General Who Supports the State, General of the Right Army, General of Agile Cavalry and army commander, and was enfeoffed Marquis of Jingling.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Yuanhui reign, by merit he reached General Who Supports the State, general of the right army, general of agile cavalry and army commander, and was enfeoffed marquis of Jingling.

sentences.zh: 沈攸之難起，太祖入朝堂，豫章王嶷代守東府，使淵領軍屯司徒左府，分備京邑。

translations.literal: When Shen Youzhi's revolt broke out, the Founder entered the hall of court; the Prince of Yuzhang, Liao, held the Eastern headquarters in his stead and had Yuan lead troops to encamp at the Minister of Public Works' left quarters, dividing forces to guard the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Shen Youzhi rose, the Founder went into the hall of court; Prince of Yuzhang Liao held the eastern headquarters in his place and set Yuan at the head of troops encamped at the minister of public works' left quarters, dividing the capital for defense.

sentences.zh: 袁粲據石頭，豫章王嶷夜登西門遙呼淵，淵驚起，率軍赴難，先至石頭焚門攻戰。

translations.literal: Yuan Can held Stone citadel; the Prince of Yuzhang, Liao, climbed the western gate at night and called Yuan from afar; Yuan sprang up in alarm, led his army to the crisis, and was first to reach Stone citadel—burning the gate and fighting through.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Can held Stone citadel; Prince of Yuzhang Liao climbed the western gate at night and hailed Yuan from afar; Yuan started up in alarm, led his host to the crisis, and was first at Stone citadel—burning the gate and fighting through.

sentences.zh: 事平，明旦衆軍還集杜姥宅，街路皆滿，宮門不開，太祖登南掖門樓處分衆軍各還本頓，至食後，城門開，淵方得入見太祖，且喜且泣。

translations.literal: When affairs were settled, at dawn the next day the armies assembled at Old Woman Du's residence; the streets were packed, the palace gates would not open, the Founder mounted the southern side-gate tower to assign each army to its own post, and only after the meal hour did the city gates open—then Yuan could enter to see the Founder, weeping for joy.
translations.idiomatic: When the affair was settled, at dawn the next day the hosts gathered at Old Woman Du's house; every street was full, the palace gates stayed shut, the Founder mounted the southern side-gate tower to send each army back to its post, and only after the meal hour did the gates open—then Yuan could enter and see the Founder, weeping between joy and relief.

sentences.zh: 太祖卽位，增邑爲二千五百戶。

translations.literal: When the Founder took the throne, Yuan's fief was increased to two thousand five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founder took the throne, Yuan's fief rose to two thousand five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 除淮陵太守，加寧朔將軍，驍騎將軍如故。

translations.literal: He was made administrator of Huailing, with added rank as General Who Pacifies the North, General of Agile Cavalry unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: He was named administrator of Huailing, with added General Who Pacifies the North, general of agile cavalry unchanged.

sentences.zh: 尋爲直閤將軍，冠軍將軍。

translations.literal: Soon he was made commander of the straight guard and General Who Commands the Champions.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made commander of the straight guard and general who commands the champions.

sentences.zh: 仍轉太子左率。

translations.literal: He was then transferred to the crown prince's left guard leader.
translations.idiomatic: He was then moved to lead the crown prince's left guard.

sentences.zh: 虜遣偽將薛道摽寇壽春，太祖以道摽淵之親近，敕齊郡太守劉懷慰曰：「聞道摽分明來，其兒婦竝在都，與諸弟無復同生者，凡此類，無爲不多方誤之，縱不全信，足使豺狼疑惑。

translations.literal: The northerners sent the false general Xue Daobiao to raid Shouchun; because Daobiao was close kin to Yuan, the Founder instructed Liu Huaishuai, administrator of Qi commandery: 「I hear Daobiao is plainly coming; his sons and daughters-in-law are all in the capital, and with his brothers he will no longer live as one family. For men of this sort, do not spare many-sided deceptions—even if they do not fully believe them, it is enough to sow doubt among the wolves and jackals.
translations.idiomatic: The northern enemy sent the false general Xue Daobiao against Shouchun; because Daobiao was Yuan's close kin, the Founder instructed Liu Huaishuai, administrator of Qi: 「I hear Daobiao is plainly on his way; his sons and daughters-in-law are all in the capital, and with his brothers he will no longer live as one household. For men like this, spare no trick from every side—even if they do not wholly believe you, it is enough to set wolves and jackals doubting one another.

sentences.zh: 」令爲淵書與道摽示購之之意，虜得書，果追道摽，遣他將代之。

translations.literal: 」He had a letter written in Yuan's name to Daobiao showing intent to win him over; the northerners got the letter, indeed recalled Daobiao, and sent another general in his place.
translations.idiomatic: 」He had a letter drafted in Yuan's name to Daobiao showing intent to buy him over; the northerners got the letter, recalled Daobiao, and sent another general in his stead.

sentences.zh: 世祖卽位，遷左衞將軍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu took the throne, Yuan was moved to General of the Left Guard.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu took the throne, Yuan was moved to general of the left guard.

sentences.zh: 初，淵南奔，母索氏不得自拔，改嫁長安楊氏，淵私遣購贖，梁州刺史崔慧景報淵云：「索在界首，遣信拘引，已得拔難。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Yuan fled south, his mother Lady Suo could not pull herself free and remarried into the Yang clan of Chang'an; Yuan privately sent men to ransom her, and Inspector of Liangzhou Cui Huijing reported to Yuan: 「Suo is at the border post; I have sent a messenger to detain and lead her out—she is already beyond the danger.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Yuan fled south, his mother Lady Suo could not break free and remarried into the Yang clan of Chang'an; Yuan secretly sent men to ransom her, and Cui Huijing, inspector of Liang, reported to Yuan: 「Suo is at the frontier post; I have sent a messenger to seize and lead her out—she is already past the danger.

sentences.zh: 」淵表求解職至界上迎之，見許。

translations.literal: 」Yuan memorialized asking to resign his post and go to the frontier to receive her; permission was granted.
translations.idiomatic: 」Yuan memorialized to resign his post and go to the border to receive her; the court granted it.

sentences.zh: 改授散騎常侍、征虜將軍。

translations.literal: He was reassigned supernumerary attendant of scattered cavalry and General Who Campaigns against the Barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned supernumerary attendant of scattered cavalry and general who campaigns against the barbarians.

sentences.zh: 淵母南歸事竟無實。

translations.literal: The matter of Yuan's mother returning south in the end had no truth to it.
translations.idiomatic: In the end the tale of Yuan's mother coming south proved untrue.

sentences.zh: ，淵上表解職送貂蟬。

translations.literal: , Yuan submitted a memorial resigning his post and sending back his court regalia.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan then memorialized to resign and sent back his court regalia.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「遠隔殊方，聲問難審。

translations.literal: The edict said: 「Separated by a distant region, word and inquiry are hard to verify.
translations.idiomatic: An edict said: 「Far apart in a foreign land, word and inquiry are hard to trust.

sentences.zh: 淵憂迫之深，固辭朝列。

translations.literal: Yuan's anguish presses deep; he firmly declines the court ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan's grief presses deep; he firmly declines the court ranks.

sentences.zh: 昔東關舊典，猶通婚宦；

translations.literal: In old precedent at the Eastern Pass, marriage and office still passed between the two sides;
translations.idiomatic: In old precedent at the Eastern Pass, marriage and office still passed between the two sides;

sentences.zh: 況母出有差，音息時至，依附前例，不容申許。

translations.literal: how much more when a mother has gone out with only a gap in degree—news reaches him from time to time; following the earlier example, his plea cannot be granted.
translations.idiomatic: how much more when a mother has gone out with only a gap in degree—news still reaches him from time to time; by the earlier example, his plea cannot be granted.

sentences.zh: 便可斷表，速還章服。

translations.literal: Let him at once withdraw the memorial and quickly return to his seals and robes.
translations.idiomatic: Let him at once withdraw the memorial and quickly return to his seals and robes.

sentences.zh: 」淵以贖母旣不得，又表陳解職，詔不許。

translations.literal: 」Because Yuan could not ransom his mother, he again memorialized to resign; the edict did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: 」Because Yuan could not ransom his mother, he again memorialized to resign; the edict would not allow it.

sentences.zh: 後虜使至，上爲淵致與母書。

translations.literal: Later when a northern envoy came, the emperor had a letter written to Yuan's mother on his behalf.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when a northern envoy came, the throne had a letter written to Yuan's mother on his behalf.

sentences.zh: 車駕幸安樂寺，淵從駕乘虜橋，先是敕羌虜橋不得入仗，爲有司所奏，免官，見原。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage visited Anle Temple, Yuan followed the procession across Qiang-barbarian Bridge; an earlier order had forbidden armed followers on that bridge—he was impeached by the relevant offices, dismissed from office, and pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial carriage visited Anle Temple, Yuan followed the procession across Qiang-barbarian Bridge; an earlier order had forbidden armed followers on that bridge—he was impeached by the relevant offices, dismissed, and pardoned.

sentences.zh: 四年，出爲持節、督徐州諸軍事、徐州刺史，將軍如故。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he went out bearing the staff, overseeing all Xuzhou military affairs, and inspector of Xuzhou, his generalship unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he went out bearing the staff, overseeing all Xuzhou military affairs and inspector of Xu, his generalship unchanged.

sentences.zh: 明年，遷右軍司馬，將軍如故，轉大司馬，濟陽太守，將軍如故。

translations.literal: The next year he was moved to right-army marshal, general as before, then made grand marshal and administrator of Jiyang, general unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he was moved to right-army marshal, general unchanged, then grand marshal and administrator of Jiyang, general still unchanged.

sentences.zh: 七年，爲給事中、右衞將軍，以疾解職。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was made offering attendant and general of the right guard, then resigned on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was made offering attendant and general of the right guard, then resigned on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 歸家，不能乘車，去車脚，使人轝之而去，爲有司所糾，見原。

translations.literal: Returning home, he could not ride in a cart; he had the cart legs removed and had men carry him away on the body—impeached by the relevant offices and pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Back at home he could not ride in a cart; he had the cart legs taken off and men carry him away on the body—impeached by the relevant offices and pardoned.

sentences.zh: 八年，爲右將軍、大司馬，領軍討巴東王子響。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was made general of the right and grand marshal, leading the army to suppress Prince Zixiang of Badong.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was made general of the right and grand marshal, leading the host to suppress Prince Zixiang of Badong.

sentences.zh: 子響軍主劉超之被捕急，以眠褥雜物十餘種賂淵自逃，淵匿之軍中，爲有司所奏，詔原。

translations.literal: Liu Chaozhi, army commander under Zixiang, was pressed in arrest and bribed Yuan with a dozen sleeping mats and other goods to escape on his own; Yuan hid him in the army—impeached, and the edict pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Chaozhi, Zixiang's army commander, was hard pressed in arrest and bribed Yuan with a dozen sleeping mats and other goods to slip away; Yuan hid him in the host—impeached, and the edict pardoned him.

sentences.zh: 十年，爲散騎常侍，將軍如故。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was made supernumerary attendant of scattered cavalry, general unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he was made supernumerary attendant of scattered cavalry, general unchanged.

sentences.zh: 世祖崩，朝廷慮虜南寇，假淵節，軍主、本官如故。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu died, the court feared a southern raid from the north and granted Yuan credentials, army commander and former rank unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu died, the court feared a southern raid from the north and granted Yuan credentials, army commander and former rank unchanged.

sentences.zh: 尋加驍騎將軍，假節、本官如故。

translations.literal: Soon he was raised to General of Agile Cavalry, with acting credentials and former rank unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was raised to general of agile cavalry, with acting credentials and former rank unchanged.

sentences.zh: ，出爲持節、督司州軍事、司州刺史，右將軍如故。

translations.literal: , he went out bearing the staff, overseeing Si Province military affairs, inspector of Si, general of the right unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: He then went out bearing the staff, overseeing Si military affairs as inspector of Si, general of the right unchanged.

sentences.zh: ，進號平北將軍，未拜，卒。

translations.literal: , he was advanced in title to General Who Pacifies the North, but before investiture he died.
translations.idiomatic: He was advanced in title to General Who Pacifies the North, but before investiture he died.

sentences.zh: 明帝卽位，方有詔賻錢五萬，布五百匹，剋日舉哀。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming took the throne, there was already an edict for funeral gift of fifty thousand cash and five hundred bolts of cloth, with mourning to begin on the set day.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming took the throne, an edict had already granted fifty thousand cash and five hundred bolts of cloth for his funeral, with mourning set for a fixed day.

sentences.zh: 戴僧靜

translations.literal: Dai Sengjing
translations.idiomatic: Dai Sengjing

sentences.zh: 戴僧靜，會稽永興人也。

translations.literal: Dai Sengjing was a native of Yongxing in Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Dai Sengjing was a man of Yongxing in Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 祖飾，宋景平中，與富陽孫法先謀亂伏法，家口徙青州。

translations.literal: His grandfather Shi: in the Jingping era of Song, he plotted rebellion with Sun Faxian of Fuyang and was executed by law; the household was relocated to Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Shi: in Song's Jingping era he plotted rebellion with Sun Faxian of Fuyang and was executed; the household was moved to Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 僧靜少有膽力，便弓馬。

translations.literal: Sengjing in youth had courage and strength, skilled with bow and horse.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Sengjing had courage and strength and was skilled with bow and horse.

sentences.zh: 事刺史沈文秀，俱沒虜。

translations.literal: He served Inspector Shen Wenxiu and together fell into northern captivity.
translations.idiomatic: He served Inspector Shen Wenxiu and together fell into northern hands.

sentences.zh: 後將家屬叛還淮陰，太祖撫畜之，常在左右。

translations.literal: Later he led his household in revolt back to Huaiyin; the Founder sheltered and nourished him, keeping him always at his side.
translations.idiomatic: Later he led his household in revolt back to Huaiyin; the Founder sheltered and kept him, always at his side.

sentences.zh: 僧靜於都載錦出，爲歐陽戍所得，繫兖州獄，太祖遣薛淵餉僧靜酒食，以刀子置魚腹中。

translations.literal: Seng Jing was hauling brocade out of the capital when Ouyang Shu seized him and had him bound in Yanzhou prison; the Founder sent Xue Yuan with food and wine for Seng Jing, with a knife hidden in a fish's belly.
translations.idiomatic: Seng Jing was carrying brocade out of the capital when Ouyang Shu took him and threw him into Yanzhou jail. The founding emperor sent Xue Yuan with food and wine, a knife tucked inside a fish.

sentences.zh: 僧靜與獄吏飲酒，旣醉，以刀刻械，手自折鏁，發屋而出。

translations.literal: Seng Jing drank with the jailers; once drunk, he used the knife to carve through his shackles, broke the locks by hand, broke through the roof, and escaped.
translations.idiomatic: He drank with the jailers until they were drunk, then carved through his fetters with the knife, snapped the locks himself, tore through the roof, and fled.

sentences.zh: 歸，太祖匿之齋內，以其家貧，年給穀千斛。

translations.literal: On his return the Founder hid him in his private quarters; because the family was poor, he granted them a thousand piculs of grain each year.
translations.idiomatic: Back in camp, the founding emperor hid him in his private quarters and, because the household was poor, gave them a thousand piculs of grain every year.

sentences.zh: 虜圍角城，遣僧靜戰盪，數捷，補帳內軍主。

translations.literal: When the northerners besieged Jiaocheng, he sent Seng Jing to strike and repel them; after several victories he was made inner-tent army chief.
translations.idiomatic: When the enemy besieged Jiaocheng, he sent Seng Jing to fight them off; after several victories Seng Jing was made chief of the inner guard.

sentences.zh: 隨還京師，勳階至積射將軍、羽林監。

translations.literal: When they returned to the capital, his merit ranks rose to General Who Accumulates Shots and Supervisor of the Feathered Forest.
translations.idiomatic: On the return to the capital his merit ranks rose to general who accumulates shots and supervisor of the feathered forest.

sentences.zh: 沈攸之事起，太祖入朝堂，僧靜爲軍主，從袁粲據石頭。

translations.literal: When Shen Youzhi's affair broke out, the Founder entered the audience hall; Seng Jing was an army chief and followed Yuan Can in holding Stone citadel.
translations.idiomatic: When Shen Youzhi's revolt broke out, the founding emperor entered the audience hall. Seng Jing was an army chief and followed Yuan Can in holding Stone citadel.

sentences.zh: 太祖遣僧靜將腹心先至石頭，時蘇烈據倉城，僧靜射書與烈，夜縋入城。

translations.literal: The Founder sent Seng Jing with his inner circle to reach Stone citadel first; at the time Su Lie held the granary city. Seng Jing shot a letter to Lie and was lowered into the city by rope at night.
translations.idiomatic: The founding emperor sent Seng Jing ahead with his trusted men. Su Lie then held the granary quarter; Seng Jing shot a letter to him and was hauled into the city by rope that night.

sentences.zh: 粲登城西南門，列燭火處分，臺軍至，射之，火乃滅，回登東門。

translations.literal: Can mounted the southwest gate of the city, arrayed torch-lights for disposition; when the palace troops arrived he shot at them, the fires went out, and he returned to mount the east gate.
translations.idiomatic: Can climbed the southwest gate and set torches to direct the fight; when the palace troops came up he shot at them, the fires went dark, and he withdrew to the east gate.

sentences.zh: 其黨輔國將軍孫曇瓘驍勇善戰，每盪一合，輙大殺傷，官軍死者百餘人。

translations.literal: His partisan, Supporting-the-State General Sun Tanhuan, was fierce and skilled in battle; every time he charged once, he would inflict heavy slaughter—a hundred and more government troops dead.
translations.idiomatic: His ally, supporting-the-state general Sun Tanhuan, was fierce in battle; every charge left a great slaughter, and more than a hundred government men fell.

sentences.zh: 軍主王天生殊死拒戰，故得相持。

translations.literal: Army chief Wang Tiansheng resisted with desperate valor, and so they were able to stalemate.
translations.idiomatic: Army chief Wang Tiansheng fought with desperate courage, and so the two sides held each other off.

sentences.zh: 自亥至丑，有流星赤色照地墜城中，僧靜率力攻倉門，身先士卒，衆潰，僧靜手斬粲，於是外軍燒門入。

translations.literal: From the hour hai to the hour chou, a crimson meteor blazed to the ground and fell within the city. Seng Jing led a forced assault on the granary gate, taking the lead before his men; the mass broke; Seng Jing personally beheaded Can, and then the outer army burned the gate and entered.
translations.idiomatic: Between the hours of hai and chou a crimson meteor flared along the ground and fell inside the walls. Seng Jing stormed the granary gate at the head of his men; the host broke; he cut down Can with his own hand, and the outer force burned the gate and poured in.

sentences.zh: 初，粲大明中與蕭惠開、周朗同車行，逢大桁開，駐車共語。

translations.literal: Earlier, during Daming in Can's day, he rode in the same carriage with Xiao Huikai and Zhou Lang; they met the Great Drawbridge open, stopped the carriage, and spoke together.
translations.idiomatic: Long before, in the Daming era, Can rode in one carriage with Xiao Huikai and Zhou Lang. The Great Drawbridge stood open; they halted and spoke together.

sentences.zh: 惠開取鏡自照曰：「無年可仕。

translations.literal: Huikai took a mirror to look at himself and said: 「No years remain in which to take office.」
translations.idiomatic: Huikai took a mirror, looked at himself, and said, 「No years are left in which to serve.」

sentences.zh: 」朗執鏡良久曰：「視死如歸。

translations.literal: Lang held the mirror a long while and said: 「To look upon death as going home.」
translations.idiomatic: Lang held the mirror a long while and said, 「I see death and return home.」

sentences.zh: 」粲最後曰：「當至三公而不終也。

translations.literal: Can spoke last: 「I shall reach the Three Dukes but not complete my course.」
translations.idiomatic: Can spoke last: 「I shall reach the three highest offices but not see the end.」

sentences.zh: 」僧靜以功除前軍將軍，寧朔將軍。

translations.literal: Seng Jing, for merit, was made General of the Forward Army and General Who Stabilizes the North.
translations.idiomatic: For merit Seng Jing was made general of the forward army and general who stabilizes the north.

sentences.zh: 將士戰亡者，太祖爲歛祭焉。

translations.literal: For officers and men who fell in battle, the Founder performed funeral rites and sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: For officers and men who died in the fighting, the founding emperor gathered the dead and made offering.

sentences.zh: ，除游擊將軍。

translations.literal: , He was made General Who Roams and Strikes.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed general who roams and strikes.

sentences.zh: 沈攸之平，論封諸將，以僧靜爲興平縣侯，邑千戶。

translations.literal: When Shen Youzhi was pacified, merit enfeoffments were debated for the generals; Seng Jing was made Marquis of Xingping with a fief of a thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: After Shen Youzhi was crushed, rewards were debated for the generals; Seng Jing was enfeoffed Marquis of Xingping at a thousand households.

sentences.zh: 太祖卽位，增邑千二百戶。

translations.literal: When the Founder took the throne, his fief was increased by twelve hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: When the founding emperor took the throne, his fief grew by twelve hundred households.

sentences.zh: 除南濟陰太守，本官如故。

translations.literal: He was made Administrator of Southern Jiyin, his former office unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: He was made administrator of southern Jiyin, his former rank unchanged.

sentences.zh: 除輔國將軍，改封建昌。

translations.literal: He was made General Who Supports the State and his title was changed to enfeoffment at Jianchang.
translations.idiomatic: He was made general who supports the state and his fief was moved to Jianchang.

sentences.zh: ，遷驍騎將軍，加員外常侍，轉太子左衞率。

translations.literal: , He was promoted to General of Valiant Cavalry, given supernumerary regular attendant, and transferred to Left Guard of the Heir.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to general of valiant cavalry, given supernumerary regular attendant, and made left guard of the heir.

sentences.zh: 世祖踐阼，出爲持節、督徐州諸軍事、冠軍將軍、北徐州刺史。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu succeeded, he went out as Bearer of the Staff, overseer of military affairs in Xu, General Who Chastises the Foe, and Governor of Northern Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu succeeded, he went out as bearer of the staff, overseer of Xu, general who chastises the foe, and governor of northern Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 買牛給貧民令耕種，甚得荒情。

translations.literal: He bought cattle and gave them to poor peasants for cultivation, winning much good will among the wasteland folk.
translations.idiomatic: He bought oxen for poor farmers to plow with and won deep goodwill among the frontier people.

sentences.zh: 遷給事中、太子右率。

translations.literal: He was moved to Palace Attendant and Right Guard of the Heir.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to palace attendant and right guard of the heir.

sentences.zh: 尋加通直常侍。

translations.literal: Soon he was given the additional title Direct-and-Plain Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was given the added title direct-and-plain regular attendant.

sentences.zh: ，隷護軍陳顯達，討荒賊桓天生於比陽。

translations.literal: , He was placed under Protector of the Army Chen Xianda to campaign against the wasteland rebel Huan Tiansheng at Biyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was placed under protector of the army Chen Xianda to campaign against the wasteland rebel Huan Tiansheng at Biyang.

sentences.zh: 僧靜與平西司馬韓孟度、華山太守康元隆前進，未至比陽四十里，頓深橋。

translations.literal: Seng Jing advanced with Pacifying-the-West staff officer Han Mengdu and Huashan Administrator Kang Yuanlong; forty li short of Biyang they halted at Shenqiao.
translations.idiomatic: Seng Jing marched with pacifying-the-west staff officer Han Mengdu and Huashan administrator Kang Yuanlong. Still forty li from Biyang, they halted at Deep Bridge.

sentences.zh: 天生引虜步騎十萬奄至，僧靜合戰大破之，殺獲萬計。

translations.literal: Tiansheng led a hundred thousand northern infantry and cavalry in a sudden onset; Seng Jing joined battle and routed them utterly, slaying and capturing by the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Tiansheng brought a hundred thousand northern foot and horse in a sudden rush. Seng Jing met them and broke them utterly, killing and capturing by the tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 天生退還比陽，僧靜進圍之。

translations.literal: Tiansheng fell back on Biyang; Seng Jing pressed on and besieged him.
translations.idiomatic: Tiansheng fell back on Biyang; Seng Jing pressed the siege.

sentences.zh: 天生軍出城外，僧靜又擊破之，天生閉門不復出，僧靜力疲乃退。

translations.literal: Tiansheng's army came outside the walls; Seng Jing defeated them again; Tiansheng shut the gates and would not come out; only when Seng Jing's strength was spent did he withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: Tiansheng's men came out beyond the walls and Seng Jing beat them again. Tiansheng shut the gates and would not stir; only when Seng Jing's strength was spent did he pull back.

sentences.zh: 除征虜將軍、南中郎司馬、淮南太守。

translations.literal: He was made General Who Campaigns Against the Barbarians, chief of staff of the Southern Central Commandant, and Administrator of Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: He was made general who campaigns against the barbarians, chief of staff to the southern central commandant, and administrator of Huainan.

sentences.zh: 八年，巴東王子響殺僚佐，世祖召僧靜使領軍向江陵，僧靜面啓上曰：「巴東王年少，長史捉之太急，忿不思難故耳。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, Prince of Badong Zi Xiang killed his staff officers; Emperor Wu summoned Seng Jing to lead troops toward Jiangling. Seng Jing spoke to the throne in person: 「The Prince of Badong is young; the chief administrator seized him too hastily—his fury outran his thought of consequences, that is all.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year Prince of Badong Zi Xiang killed his staff. Emperor Wu summoned Seng Jing to lead troops toward Jiangling. Seng Jing spoke to the throne: 「The Prince of Badong is young; the chief administrator seized him too hard. Anger outran caution, that is all.

sentences.zh: 天子兒過誤殺人，有何大罪。

translations.literal: A son of heaven who kills a man in a passing error—what grave crime is there?
translations.idiomatic: A son of heaven who kills a man in a passing fit—what grave crime is that?

sentences.zh: 官忽遣軍西上，人情惶懼，無所不至，僧靜不敢奉敕。

translations.literal: If the court suddenly sends troops west, fear will run everywhere and worse may follow; I dare not accept this order.」
translations.idiomatic: If the court suddenly sends armies west, panic will spread and worse may follow. I dare not obey.」

sentences.zh: 」上不荅而心善之。

translations.literal: The emperor did not reply but inwardly approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor gave no answer but was pleased in his heart.

sentences.zh: 徙爲廬陵王中軍司馬、高平太守，將軍如故。

translations.literal: He was shifted to staff officer of the Prince of Luling's central army and Administrator of Gaoping, his general rank unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: He was shifted to staff officer of the Prince of Luling's central army and administrator of Gaoping, his general rank unchanged.

sentences.zh: 九年，卒。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he died.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「僧靜志懷貞果，誠著艱難。

translations.literal: An edict read: 「Seng Jing's will was steadfast and his loyalty proved in hardship.
translations.idiomatic: An edict said: 「Seng Jing's will was steadfast and his loyalty stood firm through hardship.

sentences.zh: 剋殄西墉，勳彰運始。

translations.literal: He crushed the western rampart; his merit shone at the founding hour.
translations.idiomatic: He broke the western rampart; his merit shone at the dawn of the realm.

sentences.zh: 奄致殞喪，惻愴傷懷。

translations.literal: Sudden death has overtaken him; sorrow and grief wound the heart.
translations.idiomatic: Sudden death has taken him; sorrow cuts deep.

sentences.zh: 賻錢五萬，布百匹。

translations.literal: Funerary gift: fifty thousand in cash, a hundred bolts of cloth.
translations.idiomatic: Funerary gift: fifty thousand cash, a hundred bolts of cloth.

sentences.zh: 諡壯侯。」

translations.literal: Posthumous title: Marquis Zhuang.」
translations.idiomatic: Posthumous title: Marquis Zhuang.」

sentences.zh: 僧靜同郡餘姚人陳胤叔，本名承叔，避宣帝諱改。

translations.literal: Chen Yinchu of Yuyao in the same commandery as Seng Jing—his original name was Chengshu, changed to avoid the taboo of Emperor Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yinchu of Yuyao, in the same commandery as Seng Jing, had borne the name Chengshu and changed it to avoid the taboo of Emperor Xuan.

sentences.zh: 彊辯果捷，便刀楯。

translations.literal: Strong in debate, quick of hand with blade and shield.
translations.idiomatic: Sharp-tongued and quick with blade and shield.

sentences.zh: 初爲左夾轂隊將。

translations.literal: At first he was commander of the Left Flank-Chariot Company.
translations.idiomatic: At first he was commander of the left flank-chariot company.

sentences.zh: 泰始初，隨太祖東討，遂歸身隨從征伐，小心慎事，以功見賞。

translations.literal: At the opening of Taishi he followed the Founder east on campaign, then gave himself to follow on expeditions; careful and attentive in affairs, he was rewarded for merit.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Taishi reign he followed the founding emperor east on campaign, then gave himself to the field; careful in every duty, he was rewarded for merit.

sentences.zh: 封當陽縣子。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed Viscount of Dangyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed viscount of Dangyang.

sentences.zh: 官至太子左率。

translations.literal: His office rose to Left Guard of the Heir.
translations.idiomatic: His office rose to left guard of the heir.

sentences.zh: 啓世祖以鍜箭鏃用鐵多，不如鑄作。

translations.literal: He memorialized Shizu that forged arrowheads consume too much iron and are inferior to casting.
translations.idiomatic: He reported to Shizu that hammered arrowheads eat too much iron and fall short of cast work.

sentences.zh: 東冶令張候伯以鑄＜金禁＞鈍，不合用，事不行。

translations.literal: The magistrate of the Eastern Smelting Works, Zhang Houbo, found that casting, under the ban on gold in the alloy, came out dull and unfit for use; the proposal was not adopted.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Houbo of the Eastern Smelting Works tried casting, but with gold barred from the mix the points turned soft and useless, and the plan died.

translations.literal: , He died.
translations.idiomatic: Then he died.

sentences.zh: 桓康

translations.literal: Huan Kang
translations.idiomatic: Huan Kang

sentences.zh: 桓康，北蘭陵承人也。

translations.literal: Huan Kang was a native of Cheng in North Lanling.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Kang came from Cheng in North Lanling.

sentences.zh: 勇果驍悍。

translations.literal: Brave, fierce, and valiant in battle.
translations.idiomatic: He was bold, savage, and feared in the fight.

sentences.zh: 宋大明中，隨太祖爲軍容。

translations.literal: In the Daming era of Song he followed the Grand Ancestor as army equipage.
translations.idiomatic: Under Song's Daming reign he entered the Grand Ancestor's service on the army staff.

sentences.zh: 從世祖在贛縣。

translations.literal: He followed Shizu at Gan county.
translations.idiomatic: He marched with Shizu at Gan county.

sentences.zh: 泰始初，世祖起義，爲郡所縶，衆皆散。

translations.literal: At the opening of Taishi, when Shizu raised the standard, the commandery bound him and his men scattered.
translations.idiomatic: When Taishi opened and Shizu rose, the commandery seized him and his followers broke apart.

sentences.zh: 康裝檐，一頭貯穆后，一頭貯文惠太子及竟陵王子良，自負置山中。

translations.literal: Kang rigged carrying-poles: one end held Empress Mu, the other the Crown Prince Wenhu and the Prince of Jingling, Ziliang; he bore them on his back and hid them in the hills.
translations.idiomatic: Kang rigged shoulder-poles—Empress Mu in one basket, Crown Prince Wenhu and Prince Ziliang of Jingling in the other—and carried them himself into the mountains.

sentences.zh: 與門客蕭欣祖、楊瑑之、皐分喜、潛三奴、向思奴四十餘人相結，破郡獄出世祖。

translations.literal: With more than forty retainers—Xiao Xinzu, Yang Zhuanzhi, Gao Fenxi, Qian San'nu, Xiang Sinu, and the rest—he allied, broke the commandery prison, and freed Shizu.
translations.idiomatic: He joined Xiao Xinzu, Yang Zhuanzhi, Gao Fenxi, Qian San'nu, Xiang Sinu, and forty-odd other clients, smashed the county jail, and brought Shizu out.

sentences.zh: 郡追兵急，康等死戰破之。

translations.literal: Commandery pursuit troops pressed hard; Kang and his men fought to the death and broke them.
translations.idiomatic: The commandery's pursuers closed in; Kang and his band fought till they bled and drove them off.

sentences.zh: 隨世祖起義，摧堅陷陣，膂力絕人，所經村邑，恣行暴害。

translations.literal: Following Shizu in the uprising, he smashed strongpoints and broke enemy lines; his bodily strength was unmatched. In every village he passed he indulged in violence and outrage.
translations.idiomatic: On Shizu's rising he tore through walled posts and enemy arrays, and no man could match his strength. Every hamlet on his road paid in plunder and fear.

sentences.zh: 江南人畏之，以其名怖小兒，畫其形以辟瘧，無不立愈。

translations.literal: The people of the south feared him; they used his name to frighten children, and painted his likeness to ward off malaria—none failed to recover at once.
translations.idiomatic: South of the Yangtze they dreaded his name and scared children with it; they painted his figure to break malaria, and the fever always broke.

sentences.zh: 見擢爲世祖冠軍府參軍，除殿中將軍，武騎常侍，出補襄賁令。

translations.literal: He was selected as a staff officer in Shizu's champion headquarters, made Palace General and Martial Cavalry Attendant-in-ordinary, then went out to serve as magistrate of Xiangben.
translations.idiomatic: Shizu took him onto the champion staff, named him Palace General and Martial Cavalry Attendant-in-ordinary, and later sent him out as magistrate of Xiangben.

sentences.zh: 桂陽事起，康棄縣還都就太祖，會事平，除員外郎。

translations.literal: When the Guiyang affair broke out, Kang abandoned his county and returned to the capital to join the Grand Ancestor; once the crisis was settled he was made supernumerary gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: When Guiyang rose, Kang quit his post and hurried to the capital for the Grand Ancestor; after the trouble passed he received a supernumerary appointment.

sentences.zh: 元徽五年七月六日夜，少帝微行至領軍府，帝左右人曰：「一府人皆眠，何不緣牆入。

translations.literal: On the night of the sixth day of the seventh month in the fifth year of Yuanhui, the young emperor stole to the army-commander's mansion. His attendants said: 「The whole house is asleep—why not climb the wall and go in?
translations.idiomatic: On the night of the sixth of the seventh month in Yuanhui's fifth year, the young emperor slipped to the army commander's mansion. An attendant whispered: 「Everyone in the compound is asleep—why not come in over the wall?

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「我今夕欲一處作適，待明日夜。

translations.literal: 」The emperor said: 「Tonight I mean to take my pleasure in one place; wait until tomorrow night.」
translations.idiomatic: 」The boy emperor said: 「Tonight I want one bed and one woman; come back tomorrow night.」

sentences.zh: 」康與太祖所養健兒盧荒、向黑於門閒聽得其語。

translations.literal: Kang, with Lu Huang and Xiang Hei—stalwart youths the Grand Ancestor had raised—overheard their words in the doorway.
translations.idiomatic: Kang, together with Lu Huang and Xiang Hei, hard men the Grand Ancestor had reared, caught the exchange from the gate.

sentences.zh: 明夕，王敬則將帝首至，扣門，康謂是變，與荒、黑曉下，拔白欲出。

translations.literal: The next evening Wang Jingze brought the emperor's head and knocked at the gate. Kang took it for a coup; at dawn he and Huang and Hei came down, drew bare blades, and meant to break out.
translations.idiomatic: Next evening Wang Jingze arrived with the emperor's head and beat on the gate. Kang read it as revolt; at first light he, Huang, and Hei rushed down, bared steel, and were ready to cut their way out.

sentences.zh: 仍隨入宮。

translations.literal: He then followed them into the palace.
translations.idiomatic: He went in with them to the palace.

sentences.zh: 太祖鎮東府，除康武陵王中兵、寧朔將軍，帶蘭陵太守，常衞左右。

translations.literal: When the Grand Ancestor garrisoned the East Mansion, Kang was made central-troop commander for the Prince of Wuling, General Who Tranquilizes the North, and concurrent administrator of Lanling, always guarding his person.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Ancestor held the East Mansion and named Kang the Prince of Wuling's central-troop commander, General Who Tranquilizes the North, and acting prefect of Lanling, never far from his side.

sentences.zh: 太祖誅黃回，回時將爲南兖州，部曲數千，遣收，恐爲亂。

translations.literal: The Grand Ancestor executed Huang Hui. Hui was then about to take up southern Yanzhou, with several thousand retainers; when men were sent to seize him, there was fear of revolt.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Ancestor moved against Huang Hui. Hui was on the verge of southern Yanzhou with several thousand house troops; the court sent to take him in, dreading a turn.

sentences.zh: 召入東府，停外齋，使康將數十人數回罪，然後殺之。

translations.literal: Hui was summoned into the East Mansion and held in the outer quarters; Kang was told to lead several dozen men to lay out Hui's crimes, then kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Hui was called to the East Mansion and kept in the outer lodge. Kang led a few dozen men to read his offenses aloud, then struck him down.

sentences.zh: 回初與屯騎校尉王宜與同石頭之謀，太祖隱其事，猶以重兵付回而配以腹心。

translations.literal: Hui had once joined Colonel of the Martial Riders Wang Yiyu in the plot at Stone City; the Grand Ancestor concealed the matter, yet still entrusted him with a heavy force while pairing him with trusted men.
translations.idiomatic: Hui had plotted at Stone City with Wang Yiyu, Colonel of the Martial Riders; the Grand Ancestor buried the affair but still gave him a large command and set trusted men at his elbow.

sentences.zh: 宜與拳捷，善舞刀楯，回嘗使十餘人以水交灑，不能著。

translations.literal: Yiyu was quick with his fists and skilled at the dance of blade and shield; Hui once had more than ten men cross-splash him with water and not one drop could touch him.
translations.idiomatic: Yiyu was lightning with fist and shield-dance; Hui once set a dozen men to fling water at him from every side, and not a thread of him was wet.

sentences.zh: 旣慮宜與反己，乃先撤其軍將，宜與不與，回發怒不從處分，擅斬之。

translations.literal: Already fearing Yiyu would turn on him, he first stripped Yiyu of his army commanders. Yiyu would not obey; Hui in anger defied orders and executed him on his own authority.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing Yiyu would betray him, he pulled Yiyu's officers away first. Yiyu refused; Hui in a rage ignored the order and killed him outright.

sentences.zh: 諸將因此白太祖，以回握彊兵，必遂反覆。

translations.literal: The commanders therefore reported to the Grand Ancestor that Hui, gripping a strong army, would surely rebel in the end.
translations.idiomatic: The field officers then warned the Grand Ancestor that Hui, with a hard host in hand, could not stay loyal for long.

sentences.zh: 康請獨往刺之，太祖曰：「卿等何疑甚，彼無能爲也。

translations.literal: Kang asked leave to go alone and stab him. The Grand Ancestor said: 「Why do you doubt so much? He can accomplish nothing.」
translations.idiomatic: Kang offered to go in alone and run him through. The Grand Ancestor said: 「You all fret too much. He has no power left to move.」

sentences.zh: 」及回被召上車，愛妾見赤光冠其頭至足，苦捉留，回不肯止。

translations.literal: When Hui was summoned and boarded the carriage, a beloved concubine saw red light crowning him from head to foot and clung to him, begging him to stay; Hui would not stop.
translations.idiomatic: As Hui was called up and stepped into the carriage, a favorite saw a red glow from crown to heel and seized him, pleading that he stay; Hui would not be held.

sentences.zh: 時人爲之語曰：「欲侜張，問桓康。」

translations.literal: People made a saying of it: 「Want to trick Zhang—ask Huan Kang.」
translations.idiomatic: A saying ran: 「Mean to fool Zhang? Ask Huan Kang.」

sentences.zh: 除後軍將軍，直閤將軍，南濮陽太守，寧朔如故。

translations.literal: He was made Rear Army General, Direct Gate General, and administrator of southern Puyang; his rank as Tranquilizes the North stood unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: He received Rear Army General, Direct Gate General, and southern Puyang, while General Who Tranquilizes the North stayed on his tally.

sentences.zh: ，封吳平縣伯，五百戶。

translations.literal: , He was enfeoffed as Baron of Wu Ping county, with a fief of five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed as Baron of Wu Ping, with a fief of five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 轉輔國將軍，左軍將軍，游擊將軍，太守如故。

translations.literal: He was transferred to General Who Assists the State, Left Army General, and Mobile-Strike General; his prefecture was unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: He was shifted to General Who Assists the State, Left Army General, and Mobile-Strike General, still holding his prefecture.

sentences.zh: 太祖謂康曰：「卿隨我日久，未得方伯，亦當未解我意，政欲與卿先共滅虜耳。

translations.literal: The Grand Ancestor told Kang: 「You have followed me long without receiving a frontier post; you may still fail to read my mind. I mean to destroy the northerners with you first.」
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Ancestor said to Kang: 「You have marched at my side for years without a commandery of your own—you may still miss my meaning. I want you beside me when we break the northerners.」

sentences.zh: 」虜動，遣康行，假節。

translations.literal: When the northerners stirred, he sent Kang on campaign with acting credentials.
translations.idiomatic: When the barbarians moved, he sent Kang to the field with acting credentials.

sentences.zh: 尋進冠軍將軍。

translations.literal: Soon he was advanced to Champion General.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was raised to Champion General.

sentences.zh: 三年春，於淮陽與虜戰，大破之，進兵攻陷虜樊諧城。

translations.literal: In the spring of the third year he fought the northerners at Huaiyang, broke them utterly, and advanced to storm and take their fortress of Fan Xie.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year's spring he met the northerners at Huaiyang, shattered them, and pressed on to storm Fan Xie.

sentences.zh: 太祖喜，敕康迎淮北義民，不剋。

translations.literal: The Grand Ancestor was pleased and ordered Kang to welcome the loyalists north of the Huai; he could not overcome the obstacles.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Ancestor rejoiced and told Kang to bring in the righteous bands north of the Huai; he could not break through.

sentences.zh: 明年，以康爲持節、督青冀二州東徐之東莞琅邪二郡朐山戍北徐之東海漣口戍諸軍事、青冀二州刺史，冠軍如故。

translations.literal: The next year Kang was made bearer of credentials, overseer of military affairs for Qing and Ji, eastern Xu's Dongguan and Langya, the Qushan garrison, and northern Xu's Donghai and Lian Mouth garrison, and inspector of Qing and Ji; his rank as Champion stood as before.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he went out with credentials to command Qing and Ji, eastern Xu's Dongguan and Langya, the Qushan post, and northern Xu's Donghai and Lian Mouth, as inspector of both provinces—Champion still on his title.

sentences.zh: 世祖卽位，轉驍騎將軍，復前軍郡。

translations.literal: When Shizu took the throne, Kang was transferred to Valiant Cavalry General and restored to his former front-army commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: At Shizu's accession he became Valiant Cavalry General and regained his old front-army districts.

sentences.zh: 其年，卒。

translations.literal: That year he died.
translations.idiomatic: That same year he died.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「康昔預南勳，義兼常懷，倍深惻愴。

translations.literal: An edict said: 「Kang once shared in the southern merit; his loyalty was always cherished, and our grief is doubly deep.」
translations.idiomatic: The throne wrote: 「Kang stood in the southern rising; his faith was long in our hearts, and his fall cuts twice as deep.」

sentences.zh: 凶事所須，厚加料理。

translations.literal: For the funeral, generous arrangements were to be made.
translations.idiomatic: Whatever the rites required, the court would provide in full.

sentences.zh: 」年五十七。

translations.literal: He was fifty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: He was fifty-seven.

sentences.zh: 淮南人尹略，少伏事太祖，晚習騎射，以便捷見使爲將。

translations.literal: Yin Lue of Huainan had served the Grand Ancestor in youth; late in life he trained in mounted archery and, for his agility, was made a general.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Lue of Huainan entered the Grand Ancestor's household young; only later he took up bow and saddle, and his quick hand won him a general's rank.

sentences.zh: 昇明中，爲虎賁中郎、越騎校尉。

translations.literal: In the Shengming era he was Tiger-Guard Central Gentleman and Colonel of Valiant Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: In Shengming he was Tiger-Guard Central Gentleman and Colonel of Valiant Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 建元初，封平固男，三百戶。

translations.literal: At the opening of Jianyuan he was enfeoffed as Baron of Pinggu, with a fief of three hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: When Jianyuan opened he was enfeoffed as Baron of Pinggu, with three hundred households.

sentences.zh: ，爲游擊將軍，討巴東王子響，見害。

translations.literal: , He was made Mobile-Strike General, campaigned against the Prince of Badong, Zixiang, and was killed.
translations.idiomatic: He was named Mobile-Strike General, marched against Prince Zixiang of Badong, and died in the field.

sentences.zh: 贈輔國將軍、梁州剌史。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was granted General Who Assists the State and inspector of Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After death he was honored as General Who Assists the State and inspector of Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 焦度

translations.literal: Jiao Du
translations.idiomatic: Jiao Du

sentences.zh: 焦度字文續，南安氐人也。

translations.literal: Jiao Du, styled Wenxu, was a man of the Di of Nan'an.
translations.idiomatic: Jiao Du, styled Wenxu, came of the Di people of Nan'an.

sentences.zh: 祖文珪，避難至襄陽，宋元嘉中，僑立天水郡略陽縣，乃屬焉。

translations.literal: His grandfather Wen Gui fled to Xiangyang; in the Yuanjia era of the Song a migrant register was set up for Lüeyang county in Tianshui commandery, and the family was attached to it.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Wen Gui had fled to Xiangyang; under the Song, in the Yuanjia era, a migrant register was opened for Lüeyang in Tianshui commandery, and the clan was enrolled there.

sentences.zh: 度以歸國，補北館客。

translations.literal: When Du returned to the state, he was appointed a northern-lodge guest.
translations.idiomatic: After Du came home to the court, he was posted as a northern-lodge guest.

sentences.zh: 孝武初，青州刺史顏師伯出鎮，臺差度領幢主送之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaowu's reign, Yan Shibo went out to garrison as inspector of Qingzhou; the court dispatched Du as banner chief to escort him.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the reign of Emperor Xiaowu of Song, Yan Shibo took up the Qingzhou garrison; the capital sent Du as banner chief on the escort.

sentences.zh: 索虜寇青州，師伯遣度領軍與虜戰於沙溝杜梁，度身破陣，大捷。

translations.literal: The northerners raided Qingzhou; Shibo sent Du to lead troops against the enemy at Shagou Duliang; Du broke the line in person and won a great victory.
translations.idiomatic: Northerners struck Qingzhou; Shibo sent Du at the head of a column to meet them at Shagou Duliang. Du tore the enemy line apart himself and carried the day.

sentences.zh: 師伯板爲己輔國府參軍。

translations.literal: Shibo promoted him to aide on his own Supporting-the-State staff.
translations.idiomatic: Shibo raised him to an aide on his Supporting-the-State command staff.

sentences.zh: 虜遣清水公拾賁敕文寇清口，度又領軍救援，刺虜騎將豹皮公墮馬，獲其具裝鎧槊，手殺數十人。

translations.literal: The enemy sent the Lord of Clear Water, Shiben Diwen, to raid Qingkou; Du again led troops to the rescue, stabbed the northern cavalry commander Leopard-skin Duke so that he fell from his horse, seized his full barding, armor, and lance, and with his own hand killed several tens of men.
translations.idiomatic: The northerners sent the Lord of Clear Water, Shiben Diwen, against Qingkou; Du marched out again, drove his lance into the cavalry commander called Leopard-skin Duke and pitched him from the saddle, took horse-armor, mail, and lance complete, and cut down several tens of men with his own hand.

sentences.zh: 師伯啓孝武稱度氣力弓馬竝絕人，帝召還充左右。

translations.literal: Shibo reported to Emperor Xiaowu that Du's strength, bow, and horse were all unmatched among men; the emperor summoned him back to fill the personal guard.
translations.idiomatic: Shibo memorialized Emperor Xiaowu that Du's strength, bow-work, and horsemanship stood above other men; the throne recalled him to the inner guard.

sentences.zh: 見度身形黑壯，謂師伯曰：「真健物也。

translations.literal: Seeing Du's dark, stocky build, he said to Shibo: 「A truly hardy creature.
translations.idiomatic: When he saw Du's dark, thick-set frame, he told Shibo: 「What a bull of a man.

sentences.zh: 」除西陽王撫軍長兼行參軍，補晉安王子勛夾轂隊主，隨鎮江州。

translations.literal: 」He was appointed acting senior aide on the Pacifying Army staff of the Prince of Xiyang, made flank-carriage company chief for Prince Zixun of Jin'an, and followed the garrison to Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: 」He was named acting senior aide on the Pacifying Army staff of the Prince of Xiyang, made flank-carriage company chief to Prince Zixun of Jin'an, and went with the Jiangzhou garrison.

sentences.zh: 子勛起兵，以度爲龍驤將軍，領三千人爲前鋒，屯赭圻。

translations.literal: When Zixun raised arms, Du was made Dragon-soaring General, led three thousand men as vanguard, and garrisoned Zheqi.
translations.idiomatic: When Zixun rebelled, Du was made Dragon-soaring General, given three thousand men as the van, and posted at Zheqi.

sentences.zh: 每與臺軍戰，常自排突，所向無不勝。

translations.literal: Whenever he fought the court armies, he always pushed to the front himself; wherever he drove, he was never defeated.
translations.idiomatic: In every clash with the imperial host he fought at the point of the wedge himself; nothing in his path held.

sentences.zh: 事敗，逃宮亭湖中爲寇賊。

translations.literal: When the affair failed, he fled to Gongting Lake and became a bandit.
translations.idiomatic: When the cause collapsed, he took refuge on Gongting Lake and turned bandit.

sentences.zh: 朝廷聞其勇，甚憂患之，使江州刺史王景文誘降度等度，將部曲出首，景文以爲己鎮南參軍，尋領中直兵，厚待之。

translations.literal: The court heard of his bravery and was deeply troubled; they had Wang Jingwen, inspector of Jiangzhou, entice Du and his followers to surrender; Du led his band out to give themselves up; Jingwen made him his Pacifying-the-South staff officer, soon put him in charge of the central guard troops, and treated him generously.
translations.idiomatic: Word of his fighting power alarmed the court, which sent Jiangzhou inspector Wang Jingwen to lure Du and his men in. Du brought his following out to submit; Jingwen named him to his Pacifying-the-South staff, soon gave him the central guard companies, and favored him richly.

sentences.zh: 隨景文還都，常在府州內。

translations.literal: He followed Jingwen back to the capital and was constantly within the prefectural headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to the capital with Jingwen and rarely left the inspector's compound.

sentences.zh: 景文被害夕，度大怒，勸景文拒命，景文不從。

translations.literal: On the evening Jingwen was murdered, Du was furious and urged Jingwen to refuse the summons; Jingwen would not.
translations.idiomatic: The night Jingwen was killed, Du raged and pressed him to defy the order; Jingwen would not hear it.

sentences.zh: 明帝不知也。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming did not know of it.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming never learned of it.

sentences.zh: 以度武勇，補晉熙王燮防閤，除征虜鎧曹行參軍，隨鎮夏口。

translations.literal: Because of Du's martial valor, he was appointed guard to Prince Xie of Jinxi, made acting aide in the campaign-armor bureau under the General Who Punishes the Barbarians, and followed the garrison to Xiakou.
translations.idiomatic: For his fighting name he was made Prince Xie of Jinxi's household guard, named acting aide in the campaign-armor bureau, and sent with the Xiakou garrison.

sentences.zh: 武陵王贊代燮爲郢州，度仍留鎮，爲贊前軍參軍。

translations.literal: Prince Zan of Wuling replaced Xie as inspector of Yingzhou; Du remained at the garrison as front-army staff officer to Zan.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Zan of Wuling took Yingzhou in Xie's place, Du stayed on the garrison as Zan's front-army staff officer.

sentences.zh: 沈攸之事起，轉度中直兵，加寧朔將軍、軍主。

translations.literal: When Shen Youzhi's affair broke out, Du was shifted to the central guard troops, with added rank as Pacifying-the-North General and army commander.
translations.idiomatic: At the rise of Shen Youzhi, Du was moved to the central guard companies, with Pacifying-the-North General and army commander added to his title.

sentences.zh: 太祖又遣使假度輔國將軍、屯騎校尉。

translations.literal: The Grand Ancestor also sent an envoy to grant Du acting rank as Supporting-the-State General and Commandant of the Reserve Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Ancestor sent envoys as well, giving Du acting rank as Supporting-the-State General and Commandant of the Reserve Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 攸之大衆至夏口，將直下都，留偏兵守郢城而已。

translations.literal: Youzhi's great host reached Xiakou and was about to push straight to the capital, leaving only a detachment to hold Ying city.
translations.idiomatic: Youzhi's main force came up to Xiakou intending to run straight for the capital, with only a flank corps left to watch Ying.

sentences.zh: 度於城樓上肆言罵辱攸之，至自發露形體穢辱之，故攸之怒，改計攻城。

translations.literal: From the tower loft Du poured abuse on Youzhi, going so far as to bare himself and defile his body in insult; Youzhi grew angry and changed plan to besiege the city.
translations.idiomatic: Du stood on the gate tower and rained filth on Youzhi in words, then stripped and added bodily shame to the taunt. Youzhi's rage turned the march into a siege.

sentences.zh: 度親力戰，攸之衆蒙楯將登，度令投以穢器，賊衆不能冒，至今呼此樓爲「焦度樓」。

translations.literal: Du fought in person; Youzhi's men covered themselves with shields and were about to climb; Du ordered vessels of filth cast down; the rebels could not endure it; to this day the tower is called 「Jiao Du Tower.」
translations.idiomatic: Du fought hand to hand. Youzhi's men hid under shields and started up the wall; Du had ordure and night-soil hurled down until they could not climb. Men still call that tower 「Jiao Du's Tower.」

sentences.zh: 事寧，度功居多，轉後軍將軍，封東昌縣子，東宮直閤將軍。

translations.literal: When peace returned, Du's merit was greatest; he was made Rear Guard General, enfeoffed as Viscount of Dongchang, and Eastern Palace Direct Gate General.
translations.idiomatic: Once the fighting ended, his share of the credit outweighed the rest: Rear Guard General, Viscount of Dongchang, and Eastern Palace Direct Gate General.

sentences.zh: 爲人朴澀，欲就太祖求州，比及見，意色甚變，竟不得一語。

translations.literal: Plain and awkward in manner, he wished to ask the Grand Ancestor for a prefecture; by the time he came before him his expression had changed greatly, and in the end he could not get out a single word.
translations.idiomatic: Crude and tongue-tied by nature, he meant to beg the Grand Ancestor for a province; face to face, his color shifted and he never managed one sentence.

sentences.zh: 太祖以其不閑民事，竟不用。

translations.literal: The Grand Ancestor, seeing he was unversed in civil affairs, in the end did not employ him.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Ancestor judged him unfit for civil rule and let the request die.

sentences.zh: ，乃除淮陵太守，本官如故。

translations.literal: , yet he was made administrator of Huailing, his original offices unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: He was named administrator of Huailing instead, his other posts left as they were.

sentences.zh: 度見朝廷貴戚，說郢城事，宣露如初。

translations.literal: When Du met the court's great kin, he would tell of the Ying city affair, narrating the exposure just as at first.
translations.idiomatic: Among the great kin of the court he would retell the siege of Ying, baring the story again as on the tower.

sentences.zh: 好飲酒，醉輙暴怒。

translations.literal: He loved wine; when drunk he would fly into violent rage.
translations.idiomatic: He drank hard, and wine turned him savage.

sentences.zh: 上常使人節之。

translations.literal: The throne regularly sent men to restrain him.
translations.idiomatic: The court kept men at hand to check him.

sentences.zh: 年雖老，而氣力如故。

translations.literal: Though old in years, his strength was as before.
translations.idiomatic: Age did not thin his strength.

sentences.zh: 尋除游擊將軍。

translations.literal: Soon he was made General of Raiding Attack.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon named General of Raiding Attack.

sentences.zh: ，卒，年六十一。

translations.literal: , and died at sixty-one.
translations.idiomatic: He died at sixty-one.

sentences.zh: 贈輔國將軍、梁秦二州刺史。

translations.literal: Posthumously enfeoffed Supporting-the-State General and Inspector of Liang and Qin.
translations.idiomatic: After death he was honored as Supporting-the-State General and inspector of Liang and Qin.

sentences.zh: 子世榮，永明中爲巴東王防閤。

translations.literal: His son Shirong in Yongming served as guard to the Prince of Badong.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shirong, in the Yongming era, was guard to the Prince of Badong.

sentences.zh: 子響事，世榮避奔雍州，世祖嘉之，以爲始興中兵參軍。

translations.literal: When Zixiang's affair broke out, Shirong fled to Yongzhou; Shizu praised him and made him middle staff officer of Shixing.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Zixiang rebelled, Shirong ran to Yongzhou; Shizu commended him and named him middle staff officer of Shixing.

sentences.zh: 曹虎

translations.literal: Cao Hu
translations.idiomatic: Cao Hu

sentences.zh: 曹虎字士威，下邳下邳人也，本名虎頭。

translations.literal: Cao Hu, styled Shiwei, came from Xiapi in Xiapi; his original name was Hutou.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Hu, styled Shiwei, was a man of Xiapi in Xiapi; in youth he had been called Tiger Head.

sentences.zh: 宋明帝末，爲直廂。

translations.literal: At the end of Emperor Ming of Song's reign, he served in the direct side-chamber guard.
translations.idiomatic: In the last years of Emperor Ming of Song he held a post in the direct side-chamber guard.

sentences.zh: 桂陽賊起，隨太祖出新亭壘出戰，先斬一級持還，由是識太祖。

translations.literal: When the Guiyang rebels rose, he followed the Grand Ancestor out of Xinting fortress to battle, beheaded an enemy head first and carried it back—thereby coming to know the Grand Ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: When the Guiyang rebels rose, he marched with the Grand Ancestor from Xinting fortress, took an enemy head before the rest, and carried it back—by that deed he came under the Grand Ancestor's eye.

sentences.zh: 太祖爲領軍，虎訴勳，補防殿隊主，直西齋。

translations.literal: When the Grand Ancestor was Commandant of the Guards, Hu reported his merit and was appointed chief of the palace-guard company, stationed in the Western Studio.
translations.idiomatic: Once the Grand Ancestor became Commandant of the Guards, Hu laid his deeds before him and was made chief of the palace-guard company, posted to the Western Studio.

sentences.zh: 蒼梧廢明日，虎欲出外避難，遇太祖在東中華門，問虎何之？

translations.literal: On the day after the Deposed Emperor of Cangwu was removed, Hu wished to go out to escape trouble; he met the Grand Ancestor at the Eastern Central Flower Gate; the Grand Ancestor asked where Hu was going?
translations.idiomatic: The morning after the Deposed Emperor of Cangwu was cast down, Hu meant to slip out of the city; at the Eastern Central Flower Gate he met the Grand Ancestor, who asked his destination.

sentences.zh: 虎因曰：「故欲仰覓明公耳。

translations.literal: Hu thereupon said: 「I had meant only to look up and find my lord.
translations.idiomatic: Hu answered: 「I was on my way to seek you.

sentences.zh: 」仍留直衞。

translations.literal: 」He remained on direct guard.
translations.idiomatic: 」And he stayed on direct guard.

sentences.zh: 太祖鎮東府，以虎與戴僧靜各領白直三百人。

translations.literal: When the Grand Ancestor garrisoned the Eastern Mansion, Hu and Dai Sengjing each led three hundred white guards.
translations.idiomatic: When the Grand Ancestor held the Eastern Mansion, Hu and Dai Sengjing each commanded three hundred white guards.

sentences.zh: 累至屯騎校尉，帶南城令。

translations.literal: He rose by stages to Commandant of the Reserve Cavalry, with concurrent magistracy of South City.
translations.idiomatic: He climbed by stages to Commandant of the Reserve Cavalry, with South City as his concurrent magistracy.

sentences.zh: 豫平石頭，封羅江縣男，除前軍將軍。

translations.literal: In pacifying Shitou he was enfeoffed as Baron of Luojiang and made Front Army General.
translations.idiomatic: For the taking of Shitou he was enfeoffed Baron of Luojiang and named Front Army General.

sentences.zh: 上受禪，增邑爲四百戶。

translations.literal: When the throne received the abdication, the fief was increased to four hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: At the Grand Ancestor's accession his fief was raised to four hundred households.

sentences.zh: 直閤將軍，領細仗主。

translations.literal: Direct-Gate General, in charge of the fine ceremonial guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Direct-Gate General and chief of the fine ceremonial guard.

sentences.zh: 尋除寧朔將軍、東莞太守。

translations.literal: Soon he was removed as Pacifying-the-North General and Administrator of Dongguan.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he went out as Pacifying-the-North General and administrator of Dongguan.

sentences.zh: 冬，虎啓乞度封侯官，尚書奏侯官戶數殷廣，乃改封監利縣。

translations.literal: In winter Hu memorialized asking to be enfeoffed at Houguan; the Ministry memorialized that Houguan's household count was too large, and so he was enfeoffed at Jianli county instead.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Hu asked to take his fief at Houguan; the Ministry reported the place too populous for a grant, and he was given Jianli county instead.

sentences.zh: 二年，除游擊將軍，本官如故。

translations.literal: In the second year he was made General of Mobile Warfare; his original posts were unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: In year 2 he was named General of Mobile Warfare, with his former titles left as they were.

sentences.zh: 及彭、沛義民起，遣虎領六千人入渦。

translations.literal: When righteous militia rose in Peng and Pei, Hu was sent at the head of six thousand men into the Wo region.
translations.idiomatic: When loyal bands rose in Peng and Pei, Hu led six thousand men into the Wo.

sentences.zh: 沈攸之橫吹一部，京邑之絕，虎啓以自隨。

translations.literal: Shen Youzhi's horizontal-flute ensemble was a treasure unique to the capital; Hu memorialized to have it accompany him.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Youzhi's horizontal-flute band was a wonder of the capital; Hu asked leave to take it with him.

sentences.zh: 義民久不至，虎乃攻虜別營破之。

translations.literal: The righteous militia long failed to arrive; Hu thereupon attacked and broke the northerners' separate camp.
translations.idiomatic: The loyal bands never came; Hu struck instead and overran the enemy's detached camp.

sentences.zh: 將士貪取俘執，反爲虜所敗，死亡二千人。

translations.literal: Officers and men greedily seized prisoners; in turn they were beaten by the raiders, and two thousand died.
translations.idiomatic: His men stopped to plunder captives; the raiders turned on them, and two thousand fell.

sentences.zh: 世祖卽位，除員外常侍，遷南中郎司馬，加寧朔將軍、南新蔡太守。

translations.literal: When Shizu took the throne, Hu was made supernumerary attendant-in-ordinary, moved to Southern Center Army major, and given added rank as Pacifying-the-North General and Administrator of South Xincai.
translations.idiomatic: At Shizu's accession he became supernumerary attendant-in-ordinary, then Southern Center Army major, with Pacifying-the-North General and administrator of South Xincai added to his title.

sentences.zh: ，徙爲安成王征虜司馬，餘官如故。

translations.literal: , He was transferred to Campaign-against-the-Barbarians major on the Prince of Ancheng's staff; his other posts were unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: He was then shifted to Campaign-against-the-Barbarians major on the Prince of Ancheng's staff, his other offices unchanged.

sentences.zh: 明年，江州蠻動，敕虎領兵戍尋陽，板輔國將軍，伐蠻軍主。

translations.literal: The next year, when the Jiangzhou tribes rebelled, an edict had Hu lead troops to garrison Xunyang; he was appointed Supporting-the-State General and commander against the tribes.
translations.idiomatic: Next year the Jiangzhou tribes rose; the throne ordered Hu to hold Xunyang, raised him to Supporting-the-State General, and made him commander against the tribes.

sentences.zh: 又領尋陽相。

translations.literal: He also held the prefecture of Xunyang.
translations.idiomatic: He also took charge of Xunyang prefecture.

sentences.zh: 尋除游擊將軍，輔國、軍主如故。

translations.literal: Soon he was made General of Mobile Warfare; Supporting-the-State and tribal-war commander posts were unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was named General of Mobile Warfare; his Supporting-the-State rank and tribal command stayed as they were.

sentences.zh: 世祖以虎頭名鄙，敕改之。

translations.literal: Shizu found the name Tiger Head vulgar and ordered it changed.
translations.idiomatic: Shizu judged the childhood name Tiger Head coarse and commanded a change.

sentences.zh: 六年四月，荒賊桓天生復引虜出據隔城，遣虎督數軍討之。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, fourth month, the wilderness bandit Huan Tiansheng again led northerners out to hold Gecheng; Hu was sent to oversee several armies and suppress him.
translations.idiomatic: In year 6, month 4, the outlaw Huan Tiansheng once more brought raiders out to seize Gecheng; Hu was sent to command several hosts against him.

sentences.zh: 虎令輔國將軍朱公恩領騎百匹及前行踏伏，值賊遊軍，因合戰破之。

translations.literal: Hu ordered Supporting-the-State General Zhu Gong'en to take a hundred horse and vanguard scouts to feel the ground ahead; they met rebel patrols and joined battle to break them.
translations.idiomatic: Hu set Supporting-the-State General Zhu Gong'en forward with a hundred horse and scouts to probe the trail; they hit rebel patrols, closed, and routed them.

sentences.zh: 遂進至隔城。

translations.literal: Then he advanced to Gecheng.
translations.idiomatic: Then he pressed on to Gecheng.

sentences.zh: 賊黨拒守，虎引兵圍柵，絕其走路，須臾，候騎還報虜援已至，尋而天生率馬步萬餘人迎戰，虎奮擊大敗之，獲二千餘人。

translations.literal: The rebels held the defenses; Hu drew his troops around the palisade and cut off their escape. Shortly scouts returned reporting that northern reinforcements had arrived; soon Tiansheng led more than ten thousand horse and foot to meet battle; Hu struck fiercely and inflicted a great defeat, capturing more than two thousand.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels stood behind their stockade; Hu ringed the works and sealed every road out. In a moment his scouts rode back saying northern relief had come; then Tiansheng himself led ten thousand-odd horse and foot to give battle. Hu hit them head-on and broke them, taking more than two thousand.

sentences.zh: 明日，遂攻隔城拔之，斬偽虎威將軍襄城太守帛烏祝，復殺二千餘人，賊棄平氏城退走。

translations.literal: The next day he attacked Gecheng and took it, beheaded the false Tiger Might General and Xiangcheng Administrator Bo Wuzhu, killed more than two thousand again, and the rebels abandoned Pingshi city and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Next day he stormed Gecheng and carried it, beheaded the rebel Tiger Might General and Xiangcheng prefect Bo Wuzhu, cut down another two thousand, and drove the enemy from Pingshi.

sentences.zh: 七年，遷冠軍將軍，驍騎如故。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was promoted to Champion General; Valiant Cavalry was unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: In year 7 he was raised to Champion General; his Valiant Cavalry post stood.

sentences.zh: 明年，遷太子左率，轉西陽王冠軍司馬、廣陵太守。

translations.literal: The next year he was promoted to Crown Prince's Left Commander, then shifted to Champion major on the Prince of Xiyang's staff and Administrator of Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: The year after, he became Crown Prince's Left Commander, then Champion major to the Prince of Xiyang and administrator of Guangling.

sentences.zh: 上敕虎曰：「廣陵須心腹，非吾意可委者，不可得處此任。

translations.literal: The emperor edicted Hu: 「Guangling requires a trusted intimate; not someone I can entrust at will—you cannot hold this post.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told Hu: 「Guangling must go to a man at my breast—not to any officer I might name in passing. You cannot keep that post.

sentences.zh: 」隨郡王子隆代巴東王子響爲荊州，備軍容西上，以虎爲輔國將軍、鎮西司馬、南平內史。

translations.literal: 」When Prince Zilong of Suizhou replaced Prince Zixiang of Badong in Jingzhou, the court sent full military display westward and made Hu Supporting-the-State General, Pacify-the-West major, and interior administrator of Nanping.
translations.idiomatic: 」Prince Zilong of Suizhou took Jingzhou from Prince Zixiang of Badong; the court sent the full martial train west and named Hu Supporting-the-State General, Pacify-the-West major, and interior administrator of Nanping.

sentences.zh: 十一年，收雍州剌史王奐，敕領步騎數百，步道取襄陽。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year Wang Huan, inspector of Yongzhou, was seized; an edict had Hu lead several hundred foot and horse by mountain paths to take Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: In year 11 Wang Huan, inspector of Yongzhou, was taken; Hu was ordered to lead a few hundred horse and foot by back paths into Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 仍除持節、督梁南北秦沙四州諸軍事、西戎校尉、梁南秦二州刺史，將軍如故。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was made bearer of credentials, overseer of all military affairs in Liang, North and South Qin, and Sha's four provinces, Colonel of the Western Rong, and inspector of Liang and South Qin; his general posts were unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: He was then given credentials, command of the four provinces Liang, North Qin, South Qin, and Sha, the colonelcy of the Western Rong, and the two inspectorships of Liang and South Qin, while keeping his general ranks.

sentences.zh: 尋進號征虜將軍。

translations.literal: Soon he was advanced to Campaign-against-the-Barbarians General.
translations.idiomatic: Before long his title rose to Campaign-against-the-Barbarians General.

sentences.zh: 鬱林卽位，進號前將軍。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Yulin took the throne, Hu was advanced to Front General.
translations.idiomatic: At the Prince of Yulin's accession he was raised to Front General.

sentences.zh: 隆昌元年，遷督雍州郢州之竟陵司州之隨郡軍事、冠軍將軍、雍州刺史。

translations.literal: In Longchang year 1 he was moved to oversee Yongzhou and Yingzhou's Jingling and Suizhou of Sizhou military affairs, as Champion General and inspector of Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Longchang year 1 he took overall command of Yongzhou, Jingling in Yingzhou, and Suizhou in Sizhou, as Champion General and inspector of Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: ，進號右將軍。

translations.literal: , He was advanced to Right General.
translations.idiomatic: His rank was raised to Right General.

sentences.zh: 二年，進督爲監，進號平北將軍，爵爲侯，增邑三百戶。

translations.literal: In the second year his overseer post became superintendent; he was advanced to Pacify-the-North General, enfeoffed as marquis, and his fief increased by three hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: In year 2 his command became a superintendency; he was made Pacify-the-North General, enfeoffed as marquis, and given three hundred more households.

sentences.zh: 四年，虜寇沔北，虎聚軍襄陽，與南陽太守房伯玉不協，不急赴救，末乃移頓樊城。

translations.literal: In the fourth year northerners raided north of the Mian; Hu massed troops at Xiangyang, was at odds with Nanyang Administrator Fang Boyu, did not hurry to the relief, and only later shifted his camp to Fancheng.
translations.idiomatic: In year 4 the enemy struck north of the Mian. Hu held Xiangyang, quarreled with Nanyang prefect Fang Boyu, and would not march to the rescue until late, when he moved his camp to Fancheng.

sentences.zh: 虜主元宏遺虎書曰：「皇帝謝偽雍州刺史：神運兆中，皇居闡洛。

translations.literal: The northern ruler Yuan Hong sent Hu a letter: 「The Emperor thanks the false Inspector of Yongzhou: divine fortune shows at the center; the imperial dwelling opens at Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: The northern ruler Yuan Hong wrote Hu: 「The Emperor greets the pretender Inspector of Yongzhou: Heaven's mandate gathers at the center; the throne is set anew at Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 化總元天，方融八表。

translations.literal: Transformation embraces primordial Heaven; the eight directions merge as one.
translations.idiomatic: Transforming power holds the primal sky; the eight reaches melt into one realm.

sentences.zh: 而南有未賔之吳，治爲兩主之隔。

translations.literal: Yet in the south there remains unsubmissive Wu, and rule stands divided between two rulers.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Wu in the south still withholds allegiance, and the land lives under two crowns.

sentences.zh: 幽顯含嗟，人靈雍閼。

translations.literal: Spirits visible and hidden sigh together; human and divine souls are blocked in grief.
translations.idiomatic: Ghosts and men alike groan; heaven and earth are stopped in their course.

sentences.zh: 且漢北江邊，密爾乾縣，故先動鳳駕，整我神邑。

translations.literal: Moreover, north of Han and beside the river, close upon our dry county seat, the phoenix chariot moved first to order our sacred capital.
translations.idiomatic: North of the Han and along the river, hard by our royal seat, the imperial train moved first to set our sacred city in order.

sentences.zh: 卿進無陳平歸漢之智，退闕關羽殉節之忠，嬰閉窮城，憂頓長沔，機勇兩缺，何其嗟哉。

translations.literal: On the advance you lack Chen Ping's wisdom in returning to Han; on the retreat you lack Guan Yu's martyred loyalty. You shut yourself in a doomed city, weary and stalled on the long Mian—both stratagem and courage wanting. How lamentable!
translations.idiomatic: You have not Chen Ping's wit in choosing the winning side, nor Guan Yu's loyalty unto death. You cage yourself in a lost town and drag out your days on the long Mian—cunning and nerve both spent. What waste!

sentences.zh: 朕比乃欲造卿，逼冗未果，且還新都，饗厥六戎，入彼春月，遲遲揚旆，善脩爾略，以俟義臨。

translations.literal: I had lately wished to visit you, but pressing business prevented it. For now I return to the new capital to feast the six armies; when spring comes I shall slowly raise my banners. Ready your plans and await righteous arrival.
translations.idiomatic: I meant lately to come to you myself, but the press of affairs held me back. I turn now to the new capital to feast my six hosts; when spring opens I shall lift my banners in good time. Sharpen your counsel and wait on my righteous march.

sentences.zh: 」虎使人答書曰：「自金精失道，皇居徙縣，喬木空存，茂草方鬱。

translations.literal: 」Hu sent a reply: 「Since the metal essence lost the Way, the imperial dwelling moved county—tall trees stand empty while rank grass flourishes.
translations.idiomatic: 」Hu answered by messenger: 「Since the golden mandate lost its path, the throne shifted its seat—the great trunks stand bare while coarse weeds run wild.

sentences.zh: 七狄交侵，五胡代起，顧瞻中原，每用弔焉。

translations.literal: Seven Di raid in turn; five Hu rise in succession—gazing on the central plains, one must always mourn.
translations.idiomatic: Seven barbarian hosts harry the land in turn; five alien clans rise one after another—whoever looks on the central plains must mourn.

sentences.zh: 知棄皐蘭，隨水瀍澗，伊川之象，爰在茲日。

translations.literal: Knowing you abandoned Gaolan and followed the waters of Chan and Jian, the portent of the Yichuan is fulfilled this very day.
translations.idiomatic: You forsook Gaolan and went where the Chan and Jian flow—the omen of the Yichuan is fulfilled in our time.

sentences.zh: 古人有云：『匪宅是卜，而隣是卜。

translations.literal: The ancients said: 「Not the dwelling one divines, but the neighbor.
translations.idiomatic: The ancients said: 「Do not divine the house—divine the neighborhood.

sentences.zh: 』樊、漢無幸，咫尺殊風，折膠入塞，乘秋犯邊，親屬窮於斬殺，士女困於虔劉。

translations.literal: 」Fan and Han know no luck; within a spear-throw the wind differs. Frozen glue enters the passes; autumn raids the border. Kinfolk are trapped in slaughter; men and women are worn down by mass killing.
translations.idiomatic: 」Fancheng and the Han know no mercy; within a spear-cast the air changes. Ice seals the passes; you strike the frontier in autumn. Families are cut down to the last; men and women die in sweeping slaughter.

sentences.zh: 與彼蠢左，共爲脣齒，仁義弗聞，苛暴先露。

translations.literal: Joined with those blunt barbarians as lip and teeth, you hear no word of benevolence—cruelty shows first.
translations.idiomatic: You cling to those savage allies as lip to teeth, yet benevolence never reaches your lips—only cruelty comes first.

sentences.zh: 乃復改易氈裘，妄自尊大。

translations.literal: Yet again you change barbarian dress and presume to make yourself great.
translations.idiomatic: Again you trade the court robe for barbarian skins and call yourself exalted.

sentences.zh: 我皇開運，光宅區夏，而式亂逋逃，棄同卽異。

translations.literal: Our emperor opened fortune and lit the central Xia, yet you rebelliously flee and reject unity for division.
translations.idiomatic: Our emperor opened the age and brought peace to the central realm, while you run with rebels and cast off kin for strangers.

sentences.zh: 每欲出車鞠旅，以征不庭，所冀干戚兩階，叛命來格，遂復遊魂不戢，亂猾孔熾。

translations.literal: We would every time roll the war-chariots to punish the unruly, hoping weapons at the two stairs would draw rebels home—yet restless souls will not submit, and chaos runs ever wilder.
