translations.idiomatic: Again and again we would march to chastise the defiant, hoping arms laid at the two stairs would bring the wayward home—yet your restless kind will not be ruled, and disorder burns hotter.

sentences.zh: 孤總連率，任屬方邵，組甲十萬，雄戟千羣，以此戡難，何往不克。

translations.literal: I oversee allied armies, charged as frontier commander—a hundred thousand mailed men, a thousand companies of halberds—with this to quell trouble, where would we fail?
translations.idiomatic: I command the allied hosts, set as frontier marshal—mail by the hundred thousand, halberds in a thousand ranks—with such force to crush rebellion, what ground could stand?

sentences.zh: 主上每矜率土，哀彼民黎，使不戰屈敵，兵無血刃。

translations.literal: Our lord pities the realm and mourns for the people, wishing enemies to yield without battle and arms to go unstained by blood.
translations.idiomatic: Our sovereign pities the four quarters and grieves for the people, wishing foes to bow without a fight and blades to stay clean.

sentences.zh: 故部勒小戍，閉壁清野，抗威遵養，庶能懷音。

translations.literal: Therefore he arrays small garrisons, closes walls and clears the countryside, shows strength while practicing forbearance, hoping they might turn loyal.
translations.idiomatic: So he sets light guards, shuts the walls and clears the fields, shows force yet holds to restraint, hoping you may yet hear reason.

sentences.zh: 若遂迷復，知進忘退，當金鉦戒路，雲旗北掃，長驅燕代，併羈名王，使少卿忽諸，頭曼不祀。

translations.literal: If you then persist in error, knowing advance but forgetting retreat, bronze gongs will warn the road, cloud-banners will sweep north, we shall drive far through Yan and Dai, bind together the famed kings, make the young secretary suddenly gone, and Touman receive no sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: If you press on in delusion—advance without knowing when to pull back—bronze gongs will clear the march, cloud-banners will sweep the north, we shall run far through Yan and Dai, leash every crowned name among you, let your young envoy vanish in a breath, and leave Touman without offerings.

sentences.zh: 兵交無遠，相爲憫然。」

translations.literal: When arms clash, none is far; we pity one another.」
translations.idiomatic: Once steel is drawn, no land lies distant; even across the lines, men may pity each other.」

sentences.zh: ，遷給事中，右衞將軍，持節，隷都督陳顯達停襄陽伐虜。

translations.literal: , He was moved to Supervising Censor, Right Guard General, with staff of authority; placed under supervision of Regional Inspector Chen Xianda halting at Xiangyang to campaign against the barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: He was named supervising censor and Right Guard General, given staff authority, and placed under regional inspector Chen Xianda, who held at Xiangyang to fight the northerners.

sentences.zh: 度支尚書崔慧景於鄧地大敗，虜追至沔北。

translations.literal: Fiscal Director Cui Huijing suffered a great defeat at Deng; the barbarians pursued to north of the Mian.
translations.idiomatic: Fiscal director Cui Huijing was routed at Deng; the enemy chased to the north bank of the Mian.

sentences.zh: 元宏率十萬衆，從羽儀華蓋，圍樊城。

translations.literal: Yuan Hong led a host of a hundred thousand, with feathered standards and imperial parasols, and besieged Fancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Hong came in person at the head of a hundred thousand men, feathered standards and state umbrellas in train, and ringed Fancheng.

sentences.zh: 虎閉門固守。

translations.literal: Hu shut the gates and held firm.
translations.idiomatic: Hu barred the gates and stood on the defense.

sentences.zh: 虜去城數里立營頓，設氈屋，復再圍樊城，臨沔水，望襄陽岸乃去。

translations.literal: The barbarians pitched camp a few li from the city, set felt houses, again twice besieged Fancheng, faced the Mian waters, gazed toward the Yang bank of Xiangyang, and then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The northerners camped a few li out, raised felt lodges, tightened the siege of Fancheng twice, lingered on the Mian shore looking toward Xiangyang across the water, then drew away.

sentences.zh: 虎遣軍主田安之等十餘軍出逐之，頗相傷殺。

translations.literal: Hu sent more than ten army commanders such as Tian Anzhi out to pursue; they killed and wounded one another considerably.
translations.idiomatic: Hu sent Tian Anzhi and more than ten column commanders in pursuit; both sides took heavy casualties.

sentences.zh: 東昏卽位，遷前將軍，鎮軍司馬。

translations.literal: When Donghun took the throne, Hu was moved to Front General, Pacifying-the-Army staff officer.
translations.idiomatic: When Donghun ascended, Hu became front general and pacifying-the-army staff officer.

sentences.zh: ，始安王遙光反，虎領軍屯青溪中橋。

translations.literal: , When Prince Yao Guang of Shi'an rebelled, Hu led troops and camped at the Middle Bridge of Qing Creek.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Yao Guang of Shi'an rose, Hu took the field and held the Middle Bridge on Qing Creek.

sentences.zh: 事寧，轉散騎常侍、右衞將軍。

translations.literal: When the affair was settled, he was shifted to Scattered Cavalry Regular Attendant and Right Guard General.
translations.idiomatic: After order returned, he was made regular attendant of the scattered cavalry and Right Guard General.

sentences.zh: 虎形幹甚毅，善於誘納，日食荒客常數百人。

translations.literal: Hu's frame was very stern and resolute; he was skilled at winning men in; daily he fed wandering guests, usually several hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Hu was thick-set and iron-hard in bearing, clever at drawing men to him; every day he fed hired blades by the hundreds.

sentences.zh: 晚節好貨賄，吝嗇，在雍州得見錢五千萬，伎女食醬菜，無重肴。

translations.literal: In his later years he loved bribes and was stingy; in Yong province he amassed cash to the tune of fifty million; his singing girls ate pickles and greens, with no rich dishes.
translations.idiomatic: Late in life he hungered for graft and counted every cash; in Yongzhou his visible hoard reached fifty million, yet his singing girls dined on pickle and greens without a second course.

sentences.zh: 每好風景，輙開庫拍張向之。

translations.literal: Whenever he loved the scenery, he would open the treasury and perform hand-clap toward it.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever a view pleased him, he opened the storehouse and called for hand-clap players to perform toward it.

sentences.zh: 帝疑虎舊將，兼利其財，新除未及拜，見殺。

translations.literal: The emperor suspected Hu as an old commander and coveted his wealth; before he could attend his new appointment he was killed.
translations.idiomatic: The throne mistrusted an old fighting man and coveted his hoard; Hu was cut down before he could take up his new post.

sentences.zh: 時年六十餘。

translations.literal: He was then a little over sixty.
translations.idiomatic: He was a little past sixty.

sentences.zh: 和帝中興元年，追贈安北將軍、徐州刺史。

translations.literal: In the first year of the Zhongxing restoration under Emperor He, he was posthumously granted General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Emperor He's Zhongxing restoration, he was posthumously named General Who Pacifies the North and inspector of Xuzhou.

translations.literal: Appraisal
translations.idiomatic: Appraisal

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：解厄鴻門，資舞陽之氣；

translations.literal: The historian writes: To escape crisis at Hong Gate drew on Wuyang's spirit;
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: crisis broken at Hong Gate rested on Wuyang's nerve;

sentences.zh: 納降饗旅，仗虎侯之力。

translations.literal: to receive surrender and feast the army relied on the Tiger Marquis's strength.
translations.idiomatic: to take surrender and feast the host leaned on the Tiger Marquis's force.

sentences.zh: 觀茲猛毅，藉以風威，未必投車挾輈，然後勝敵。

translations.literal: Seeing such fierce resolve, aided by martial prestige, one need not overturn chariots and seize reins before defeating the foe.
translations.idiomatic: Men of such fighting nerve, backed by martial dread, need not overturn chariots and seize reins before they win.

sentences.zh: 故桓康之聲，所以震懾江蠡也。

translations.literal: Hence Huan Kang's name could awe the river pests.
translations.idiomatic: That is why Huan Kang's name alone could cow the Yangtze scourge.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：薛辭親愛，歸身淮涘。

translations.literal: In praise: Xue left family affection and gave himself to the Huai shore.
translations.idiomatic: In praise: Xue turned from kin and pledged himself to the Huai bank.

sentences.zh: 戴類千秋，興言帝子。

translations.literal: Dai's kind lasts a thousand autumns; his words stirred the emperor's sons.
translations.idiomatic: Dai's sort endures a thousand years; his counsel moved the imperial sons.

sentences.zh: 桓勇焦壯，爪牙之士。

translations.literal: Huan brave as Jiao strong—a fang-and-claw man.
translations.idiomatic: Huan bold as Jiao stout—a teeth-and-claw fighter.

sentences.zh: 虎守西邊，功虧北鄙。

translations.literal: Hu guarded the western marches; merit failed on the northern border.
translations.idiomatic: Hu held the western frontier; credit broke on the northern line.
